title: Job classes that are paid but appear in neither published pay table
question: Which job classes had paid holders in the latest year but no step or range in either pay table the City publishes?
finding: 6 job classes with 688 paid holders in fiscal 2026 have no rate in either published pay table; they were paid $21.4 million. The largest are Technology Expert I (class 9976) (64 holders, $11.0 million), Public Service Trainee (class 9910) (612, $7.9 million) and Transitional Department Head (class 0971) (4, $1.1 million).
how: Every class with a paid holder in fiscal 2026 is looked up, at any date, in the Hourly Rates of Pay by Classification and Step table (fiscal 2015 to 2026) and the City Employment Compensation Plan (steps and ranges from 2020). Listed: classes found in neither. “On the payroll since” is the first fiscal year anyone was paid in the class, back to 2013. Board seats, elected offices and the Superior Court are left out. Ranked by pay.
limits: A class can be missing from the tables because its pay is set case by case under an individual contract, because it is paid a flat or per-meeting amount, or because the tables as published are incomplete. None of that is improper, but it means the public cannot check the pay against a scale. The job-classification database would show whether each class has a pay grade and how it is set.
